name: Blue Gum Creek.....but with a difference!
description:
Who Is Leading - Keith Dyson 

Rated: Medium Hard. Suitable for rough terrain bushwalkers.

Meet Time: 0800, at Paluma. Meet point will be disseminated to registered participants

Duration: Full day walk. will be back at the cars by 5:00 pm. 

Description:

Based on the traditional Blue Gum Circuit track walk, but with several short off-track adventures to
waterfalls we rarely visit. This time of year the waterfalls and cascades are flowing well so should be
spectacular.
 
Terrain:  
Steep ascents / descents (including 400 mr ascent on way home). Mostly rough forest track
walking, but includes rockhopping on potentially slippery rocks in the creeks, and some off-track
bushbashing. The walking includes steep descents / ascents, slippery rocks, trip hazards, tangled
vines and jungle, wait-a while, risk of cuts and scratches from jungle vegetation, creek wading, rock
hopping, and uneven footings.

What to bring:

Footwear – due to wet conditions and creek wading, shoes that are suitable for getting wet and wading in water is recommended.
Water: 3-4 litres. Sterilisation tablets if you’re planning to refill your water from creeks
-Electrolytes as needed
-Sunscreen & hat
-Insect repellent
-Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces
-Dry clothes and maybe thongs for after the walk
-Swimming togs & towel if planning to swim
-Trail snacks, morning tea and lunch
-Salt for leeches
-Rain poncho
-Camera
-First-aid kit and snake bite bandage, whistle
 
Must be over 18 years to participate.
Non-members (Visitor) fee $5.

For walk briefing, or for more info, contact Keith direct at kadyson@hotmail.com

name: Unnamed Waterfalls
description:
Next bushwalk - Unnamed Waterfall, Girringun National Park

An off-track remote wilderness exploratory adventure.
Continuing our recent theme of off-track wilderness exploring, this Saturday we try this remote waterfall.
Duration - Two days
Require camping gear
Rated - Hard.
Pre-Registration / approval with the walk leader is essential. Register ASAP to reserve a spot.
For more info, contact the club info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com
Leader: Luen Warneke 
Meet: 6:00am - ask the walk leader for location once registered. 
REGISTER: https://forms.gle/hpmys1E9naaP1Yhx6

Secateurs are mandatory!!!


This is a remote rainforest creek bushwalk. You may be walking in the water, there will be slippery rocks, uneven footing, slippery tree roots, tangled vines, lots of waot-a-while and gimpie gimpie, all that good fun adventure. The rewards are great scenery, adventure, a sense of achievement, and great company. See photos on the club's Facebook or Luen's website wanderstories.space for examples of potential bushwalking conditions from the recent creek based exploratory adventures.

From Wallaman Falls, we drive and hike down the creek to the top of a hidden waterfall. 3 km one way, which will take all day due to the thick vegetation.

Fully wo days hike, anticipate back at the cars around 5 pm Sunday depending on conditions and group.
Wear appropriate footwear, i.e., enclosed sturdy shoes that grip on slippery rocks.
Drinking water - carry 1-2 lt, refill from creeks as required (but suitably treat/filter any water refills from natural sources, or carry 3+ lt). The club also recommends use of electrolytes during the day.
Bring food and snacks to suits your energy needs for the bushwalking.
Bushwalkers should bring their own personal (minimal) first aid kit, headtorch, and whistle. 
Own camping gear, etc.
Luen will also have his personal minimal first aid kit and PLB. The club does not provide a group first aid kit.
Fees: non-members $5
Clothing- as it off-track bushwalking, long sleeve clothing or gaiters is recommended. Otherwise you may have sun burn and cuts/scratches on exposed skin at the end of the day.
Must be over 18yrs to participate.

name: Dolby Creek and Junction (Spa) Falls
description:
Dolby Creek and Junction (Spa) Falls 

One day Bushwalk

Sunday 12th Feb 2023  

Leader - Keith 

Rated – Medium Hard. Suitable for rough terrain bushwalkers.

Meet – Time 0730, at Paluma. Meet point will be disseminated to approved registered participants. 

Maximum participants -15

Mt Spec Section, Paluma Range National Park - A spectacular rainforest creek full day walk. Hike on rainforest tracks to Dolby Creek, then bushbashing and wading along creek lines. Hike past cascades and secret pools, to a great waterfall and pool (off track) in the Paluma Range National Park. Track route home will be decided on the day. 

Terrain - The off-track bushbashing includes slippery rocks, tangled vines and  jungle, wait-a while, creek wading, rock hopping, and uneven footings. Some moderate hills are climbed.

Footwear – due to wet conditions and creek wading, shoes that are suitable for getting wet and wading in water is recommended. 

Must be over 18 years to participate. 

Non-members (Visitor) fee $5.

Drinking Water – bring water for a full day bushwalking. Refill from creeks is readily available, but the club recommends that water resupply from natural sources is suitably treated before consumption. 

Anticipate being back in Paluma around 5:30pm.  

For walk briefing, to register, or for more info, contact the Club info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com
Register form: 
https://forms.gle/G7yJpnCEcR8RFvvN6

Please read ‘Walker Guidelines’ and ‘What to Bring’ at these links: 

Walker Guidelines - Townsville Bushwalking Club 
https://www.townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/about/walker-guidelines
Walk Together - Townsville Bushwalking Club 
https://www.townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/about/walk-together
What to Bring? - Townsville Bushwalking Club

Bring insect repellent (leeches, mozzies). 

Walker registration approval is conditional on approval by the activity leader. Note that cub members are given priority at the leader's discretion.

name: Saddle Creek, Paluma
description:
Next bushwalk - Saddle Creek, Paluma - 04/02/23

An off-track remote wilderness exploratory adventure.
Continuing our recent theme of off-track wilderness creek-based exploring in the Paluma area, this Sunday we try Saddle Creek.
Rated - Hard.
Pre-Registration / approval with the walk leader is essential. These walks have been very popular, so register ASAP to reserve a spot.
For more info, contact the club info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com
Meet: 7:30am - ask walk leader for location once registered. 
REGISTER:
https://forms.gle/VHE7uM6CnJoN9aJRA

This is a remote wilderness creek bushwalk. You may be walking in the water, there will be slippery rocks, uneven footing, slippery tree roots, tangled vines, all that good fun adventure. The rewards are great scenery, fun adventure, good laughs, a sense of achievement, and great company. See photos on the club's Facebook or Luen's website wanderstories.space for examples of potential bushwalking conditions from the recent creek based exploratory adventures.

From The Saddle on the Paluma Range Road, hike down the creek to Spiegelhauer Road. 3 km one way.

Half day hike, anticipate back at the cars around 12-2 pm depending on conditions and group.
Wear appropriate footwear, i.e., enclosed sturdy shoes that grip on slippery rocks.
Drinking water - carry 1-2 lt, refill from creeks as required (but suitably treat/filter any water refills from natural sources, or carry 3+ lt). The club also recommends use of electrolytes during the day.
Bring food and snacks to suits your energy needs for full day bushwalking.
Bushwalkers should bring their own personal (minimal) first aid kit, headtorch, and whistle. Luen will also have his personal minimal first aid kit. The club does not provide a group first aid kit.
Fees: non-members $5
Clothing- as it off-track bushwalking, long sleeve clothing or gaiters is recommended. Otherwise you may have sun burn and cuts/scratches on exposed skin at the end of the day.
Must be over 18yrs to participate.
Now you might think we will be running out of wilderness creeks to explore around Mt Spec - well, we won't, there are many more unique ideas we have in plans.
